key_insight: A heavy-hexagon-specific defect-avoidance circuit can route around faulty qubits and measurably lower logical error rates on real superconducting hardware.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical fault-tolerance strategy for low-connectivity quantum processors where fabrication or calibration defects cannot be ignored.
method: Identify defective physical qubits in the heavy-hexagon lattice.
Redesign stabilizer/gauge measurements to avoid the defect using a two-cycle measurement schedule.
Implement and test the defect-avoidance circuits on IBM quantum hardware.
evidence_signal: Hardware experiments reported about a 10% reduction in logical error rate per cycle for both logical X and Z errors when defects were avoided.
watch_item: The approach is tailored to the specific heavy-hexagon connectivity and still depends on accurate defect detection and circuit reconfiguration.
